title: Chrome saved passwords
whyItMatters: Holds every username and password saved in Chrome. The values are encrypted with the Windows account, but scripts that can run as that user can decrypt them.
source: Chromium user data directory docs, profile files include Login Data: https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/docs/user_data_dir.md
notes: One Login Data file per profile. Delete it through Chrome (passwords settings) or the profile stays signed in and repopulates it.

cleanup.exportFirst: In Chrome, open Settings > Autofill and passwords > Google Password Manager and use Export passwords to save them to a file you keep.
cleanup.signOut: In Chrome, open Settings > You and Google and turn off sync, so the account stops keeping this PC in step.
steps: Delete the saved passwords in Chrome only if you want them gone from your Google account too; otherwise skip this step.
Delete the login data file named in the plan if it is still there.
cleanup.risk: Without the export, every password saved in Chrome is lost; while the profile stays signed in, sync can restore the file.
cleanup.source: Google Chrome Help, Manage passwords in Chrome: https://support.google.com/chrome/answer/95606
